---
title: "JQI_AIWorry_PlotConstruction"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# =========================================================
# 2024 AI WORRY BY RACE
# Compensation, Benefits, and Earnings Stability
# White vs. Black respondents
# =========================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load packages
# ---------------------------------------------------------

library(gssr)
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(broom)
library(here)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the full GSS cumulative file
# ---------------------------------------------------------

data(gss_all)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Extract the 2024 GSS variables we need
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_aiworry <- gss_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    id,
    aiworry,
    racecen1,
    indus10,
    wrkstat,
    class
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct common BLS industry categories
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_aiworry <- gss_aiworry %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(indus10)
    ),
    
    industry_common = dplyr::case_when(
      
      indus10_num == 770 ~ "Construction",
      
      indus10_num >= 1070 &
        indus10_num <= 3990 ~ "Manufacturing",
      
      indus10_num >= 4070 &
        indus10_num <= 4590 ~ "Wholesale trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 4670 &
        indus10_num <= 5790 ~ "Retail trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 6070 &
        indus10_num <= 6390 ~ "Transportation and warehousing",
      
      indus10_num >= 6470 &
        indus10_num <= 6780 ~ "Information",
      
      indus10_num >= 6870 &
        indus10_num <= 6990 ~ "Finance and insurance",
      
      indus10_num >= 7070 &
        indus10_num <= 7190 ~ "Real estate and rental and leasing",
      
      indus10_num >= 7270 &
        indus10_num <= 7490 ~ "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7570 &
        indus10_num <= 7790 ~ "Administrative and support and waste management",
      
      indus10_num >= 7860 &
        indus10_num <= 7890 ~ "Educational services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7970 &
        indus10_num <= 8470 ~ "Health care and social assistance",
      
      indus10_num >= 8560 &
        indus10_num <= 8690 ~ "Leisure and hospitality",
      
      indus10_num >= 8770 &
        indus10_num <= 9290 ~ "Other services",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Load the underlying job-quality measures
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_primary <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Construct the three JQI components
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_for_gss <- job_quality_primary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # Compensation
    z_wage_premium = as.numeric(
      scale(wage_premium)
    ),
    
    z_wage_cost = as.numeric(
      scale(wage_cost_per_hour)
    ),
    
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_wage_cost
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Benefits
    z_benefits = as.numeric(
      scale(benefits_nonrequired)
    ),
    
    benefits = z_benefits,
    
    # Earnings stability
    # Higher = more stable
    z_earnings_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-earnings_volatility)
    ),
    
    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability,
    
    # Composite JQI
    jqi_primary = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    industry_common,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability,
    jqi_primary
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Merge job quality onto the 2024 GSS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_aiworry <- gss_aiworry %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    job_quality_for_gss,
    by = c(
      "year",
      "industry_common"
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Construct employment-status and social-class factors
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_aiworry <- gss_aiworry %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    wrkstat_factor = factor(
      wrkstat,
      levels = 1:8,
      labels = c(
        "Full-time",
        "Part-time",
        "Temporarily not working",
        "Unemployed",
        "Retired",
        "In school",
        "Keeping house",
        "Other"
      )
    ),
    
    social_class_factor = factor(
      class,
      levels = 1:4,
      labels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    ),
    
    race_group = dplyr::case_when(
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c(
        "White",
        "Black"
      )
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Keep White and Black respondents with complete data
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_aiworry_race <- gss_aiworry %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    race_group %in% c(
      "White",
      "Black"
    ),
    !is.na(aiworry),
    !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
    !is.na(social_class_factor),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  )


# Check sample sizes
gss_aiworry_race %>%
  dplyr::count(race_group)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Estimate race-specific ordered-logit models
# ---------------------------------------------------------

aiworry_white <- MASS::polr(
  ordered(aiworry) ~
    wrkstat_factor +
    social_class_factor +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = gss_aiworry_race %>%
    dplyr::filter(race_group == "White"),
  Hess = TRUE
)


aiworry_black <- MASS::polr(
  ordered(aiworry) ~
    wrkstat_factor +
    social_class_factor +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = gss_aiworry_race %>%
    dplyr::filter(race_group == "Black"),
  Hess = TRUE
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Extract JQI coefficients and confidence intervals
# ---------------------------------------------------------

aiworry_race_coefficients <- list(
  White = aiworry_white,
  Black = aiworry_black
) %>%
  purrr::imap_dfr(
    ~ broom::tidy(
        .x,
        conf.int = TRUE
      ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        term %in% c(
          "compensation",
          "benefits",
          "earnings_stability"
        )
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        race_group = .y
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    component = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      compensation = "Compensation",
      benefits = "Benefits",
      earnings_stability = "Earnings stability"
    ),
    
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c(
        "Compensation",
        "Benefits",
        "Earnings stability"
      )
    ),
    
    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c(
        "White",
        "Black"
      )
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Inspect the coefficients
# ---------------------------------------------------------

aiworry_race_coefficients %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race_group,
    component,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Create coefficient plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

aiworry_race_plot <- ggplot(
  aiworry_race_coefficients,
  aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = component
  )
) +
  
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      xmin = conf.low,
      xmax = conf.high
    ),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  
  geom_point(
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(
    ~ race_group,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Ordered-logit coefficient",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Job Quality and AI Worry by Race",
    subtitle = "2024 GSS; adjusted for employment status and social class"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 13
  ) +
  
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Display plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

aiworry_race_plot


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Save plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "aiworry_jqi_race_coefficients.png"
  ),
  aiworry_race_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 5.5,
  dpi = 300
)
```
